learning: Iteration 4 changes sensor pitch, track and mass together, and kp slightly. The s-bend result is the cleanest read of the drivetrain change because it has no line loss. The slalom line-loss count reflects the pitch change. If s-bend progress rises but the slalom still loses the line, the pitch was too narrow. If the robot oscillates, the gain or the track change is the cause.
notes: Complete package for the Builder's iteration 4 proposal: 16 mm sensors at 20 mm pitch (±0.06 m), wheel_track 0.10 m, mass 0.6 kg. kp is set to 5.5 to hold steering gain across the wider span while allowing for the higher turn rate of the narrower track. Weights remain proportional to x.
rationale: Iteration 2 (16 mm contiguous sensors at x = ±0.048 m, kp 5.0) removed line loss on the oval and s-bend, so the footprint change works. Iteration 3 repeated that geometry with kp 5.0 and returned identical metrics, so gain alone does not move the s-bend. The s-bend stays at progress 0.04 with max_error 0.0611 m and zero line loss, so the robot is drifting through turn-rate lag. The slalom still loses the line once per run at max_error 0.0628 m, which means the 4 to 5 cm error zone is not fully covered. I adopt the Builder's proposal exactly: 16 mm sensors at 20 mm pitch (x = -0.06 to +0.06 m, y = 0.03 m), wheel_track 0.10 m, mass 0.6 kg. Body width and length are unchanged. Weights stay proportional to x (-1.0 to +1.0), so a positive signal steers left as the contract requires. The wider span lowers the signal per metre of error from about 104 per metre (kp 5.0 over 0.048 m) to about 83 per metre at 0.06 m. Holding that gain needs kp near 6.2. The narrower track raises turn rate per unit of turn by about 20 percent, which pushes the other way. I therefore set kp to 5.5, a compromise that keeps steering authority near the earlier level without overshooting. ki stays at 0.05 and kd at 0.3. The change list is wider pitch, narrower track, lower mass and a small kp change. The next race will confound these, so the feedback names which result points to which lever.
